seoTitle: Why Is My Neon Sign Flickering? Diagnostic & Fix Guide
seoDescription: Why is your neon sign flickering? Learn how to diagnose failing 12V power adapters, loose DC barrel plugs, PWM dimmer faults, and camera shutter conflicts.
summary: A flickering LED neon sign is caused by a failing 12V power supply in roughly 70% of cases, followed by a loose DC barrel connector, a failing inline PWM dimmer, or an overloaded circuit. For traditional glass neon, flickering stems from a dying high-voltage transformer, arcing GTO wiring, or depleted neon gas. Isolating the fault takes five minutes using a direct power bypass test.
secondaryKeywords: why is my neon sign flickering
how to fix flickering neon sign
keyTakeaways: Test the power adapter first by unplugging inline dimmers and remote receivers to connect the power supply directly to the sign's DC input jack.
If the sign strobes or shuts down after 2 to 5 minutes of operation, the power adapter is overheating or undersized and tripping its internal thermal cut-off.
Flickering that only appears on smartphone video or camera screens is caused by low-frequency PWM dimming conflicting with camera shutter speeds, not a hardware fault.
Traditional glass neon signs operate at 2,000 to 15,000 volts; loud buzzing or visible sparks indicate high-voltage transformer arcing that requires certified electrical service.
When replacing a power supply, always match the exact output voltage (12V or 24V DC) and provide at least 20% wattage headroom above the sign's total draw.
